provenance.install: cargo install vaultlint --version 0.2.0 --root <root>, binary at <root>/bin/vaultlint, version confirmed by `vaultlint --version` = 0.2.0 before the run
provenance.install_documented_at: the crate's crates.io page and repository README, which document `cargo install vaultlint`; the version pin is the registry's own 0.2.0, published 2026-09-25
provenance.note: Release v0.2.0, release commit fbc5a8e8eaa46b713a7feeaea54b2530652a8c9c, detected by the rules-drift watch the same day. The 0.1.1 row is not overwritten: this is a second, versioned row beside it, scored with the same pre-registered mappings/vaultlint.json. Measured outside a container (no docker engine in the measuring sandbox); the binary is pinned by version from the registry, and the invocation is the same two-pass shape the 0.1.1 docker row used.

run.invocation_evidence: Same two-pass shape as the 0.1.1 row (adapters/vaultlint.json, recovered 2026-09-01 from raw/vaultlint-c2-2026-09-01/): the human formatter goes to stderr for the coverage line, the json pass to stdout for findings. Read off the binary itself on 2026-09-25: `vaultlint scan --help` shows --format human|json|sarif and --fail-on high|medium|low|never; a smoke run against a corpus leaf prints '→ analyzing 1 Rust file (Anchor 0.20.1) …', which is the line the coverage evidence pattern matches, and the JSON envelope is {findings: [{rule_id, file, line, column, ...}], skipped: []}. --mainnet was read from --help and deliberately NOT passed: the network-hermetic default is the 0.1.1 baseline this row is compared against, and the release notes say the default makes no network calls.

evidence.means: vaultlint's own count of the files it opened, printed by its human formatter before it analyses them and before it says whether it found anything

findings.message: Account data is deserialised without an owner check

measurements.note: v0.2.0 re-measurement of the teaching corpus at the same pinned commit 24555d044802db4022112a94d6d70e74291a4b6d, 35 leaves, run per-case through the framework with --repeat 2. Scored with the 0.1.1 pre-registered mapping (mappings/vaultlint.json, committed 2026-08-31, unedited): the release changed which findings the tool emits, not what its rule ids mean. v0.2.0's ungated VL003 (missing overflow-checks now reported without waiting for arithmetic) is a manifest-level project finding; on this harness each leaf's workspace root is the corpus repository's own root manifest, which sits above the per-leaf scan root, and no leaf manifest declares its own [workspace], so the ungated VL003 cannot fire here - the delta on this corpus is zero by construction, and that is written down rather than left to be rediscovered.
